page.text:
Quantifier order records dependence. The statement
$\forall x\,\exists y\,R(x,y)$ permits the witness $y$ to depend on $x$;
the statement $\exists y\,\forall x\,R(x,y)$ requires a single witness
that works uniformly for all $x$. The second statement implies the first
when the domains are nonempty, but the converse generally fails. This
distinction later reappears in uniform continuity, where one $\delta$
must work simultaneously at every point of a domain.
